title: React UI: Expandable Support Answers
businessContext: A compact support panel should expose one answer at a time while remaining usable with native keyboard controls.
problemStatement: Export App({ items = [] }). Each item has unique id, title, and body strings. Render a heading button per item, initially all collapsed. Activating a collapsed button opens its body and closes the previously open body; activating the same button collapses it. Each button needs aria-expanded and aria-controls="panel-ID". An open body is a region with id="panel-ID" and aria-labelledby referring to its button id="trigger-ID". Only open regions exist in the DOM. An empty array shows No help articles in [data-testid="empty"]. Use native buttons rather than clickable divs.
constraints: Item IDs are unique, nonempty, HTML-id-safe strings; titles and bodies are plain text.
Use stable item IDs for keys and open state, not array positions.

testCases.name: Empty configuration has a useful state
Opening creates a labelled answer region
Opening another answer closes the first
Activating an open heading collapses it

hints: One open ID or null expresses the single-open invariant.
Derive aria-expanded from the same equality used to render the region.
commonMistakes: Keeping an independent open flag on each row, violating single-open behavior.
Rendering a visually hidden panel that still violates the specified DOM contract.
candidateTasks: Implement the default-exported App component and the documented DOM contract.
Run every interaction journey, explain edge cases, then compare your implementation with the reference.
alternativeApproaches: Extract a small pure helper for derived values; keep input state in the component. Extend with a custom hook only when behavior is reused.
